purpose: Screen ascending expert-ID work ordering inside the existing fused multi-token MMVQ kernel
hypothesis: Matching experts at the same sorted rank could improve intra-block weight reuse without MMQ packing or loss of gate/up fusion
input: Previously captured complete Rust and JSON routes from routed-overlap-20261021, not new or independent samples
transformation: Sort each token's selected experts by ascending expert ID. A future kernel must retain the inverse permutation for original activation/output slots, preserving graph tensors and arithmetic order.
phase: Four-token target verification only; exclude the initialization frame and both prefill frames, including the four-token prompt tail

opportunity_gate.requirement: Both development prompts must meet the threshold before considering a CUDA prototype
opportunity_gate.meaning: Logical reuse triage only, not a predicted speedup, DRAM-traffic estimate or proof of cache reuse

validation: Reconcile records against original log lines and published phase/token counts
Reproduce published original same-rank and global overlap totals exactly
Verify each permutation is bijective and preserves the original expert-to-output-slot mapping
Check synthetic disjoint, already-aligned and differently-ranked identical expert sets
stop_rule: If either case fails, stop this ascending-ID ordering hypothesis without alternative order heuristics, per-layer subsets, CUDA builds or model runs
limitations: Sorting instruction cost and physical cache behavior are not measured
Existing cache reuse may already capture the opportunity
The two single-sequence development prompts do not establish generality or multi-sequence correctness
